suSSHi Chef Config API

API Endpoint
https://susshi.io

API Usage ¶

The config REST (Representational State Transfer) API is a feature-rich API to configure suSSHi Chef with all its contents.

The API is accessible on the base URL /api/v1/config. All model specific resource paths are organized under this base URL and can be accessed accordingly.

About ¶

This documentation represents the API of suSSHi Chef Version 18.03 (and later) and contains details about all Config API resources and their HTTP methods together with example data and schema definitions for the request and respons bodys.

HTTP methods ¶

The https-based suSSHi Chef Config API, which is a stateless protocol, uses secure HTTP methods to provide CREATE, READ, UPDATE and DELETE (CRUD) operations on the model abstractions of data stored within suSSHi Chef’s database.

HTTP method Data method
GET Retrieve a list of objects or a single object in a JSON representation
POST Create a new object with the data provided in the body in a JSON representation
PUT Update an existing object with the data provided in the body in a JSON representation, only given attributes are updated
PATCH Modify an existing object by adding or removing elements to contained objects / object relationships, only given attributes are updated
DELETE Destroy an existing object

Resources ¶

REST APIs use Uniform Resource Identifiers (URIs) to address resources. In REST, a primary data representation is called Resource. Having a strong and consistent REST resource naming strategy is proved to be a good design decision in long term.

A resource can be a singleton or a collection. For example, susshi_users is a collection resource and susshi_user is a singleton resource.

  • We can identify susshi_users collection resource using the URI /api/v1/config/susshi_users for all kind of suSSHi Users or /api/v1/config/susshi_users/logins for Login Users only.

  • We can identify a single susshi_user resource using the URI /api/v1/config/susshi_users/logins/{id} where id is the primary key ID used in the database to uniquely identify this object.

In the suSSHi Chef Config API, for most resources an id can also be replaced with name which acts like a second unique identifier for the object since most models do not allow to have the same name twice, e.g. the susshi_user with username “john” can only exist once in the database regardless of what ID it has.

A resource may contain a “sub class” within the corresponding model to address specific kinds of the model. For example, “source_ips” are just a top class of the sub classes “networks” and “groups” which can then be addresses with /api/v1/config/source_ips/nets or /api/v1/config/source_ips/groups accordingly. Please refer to the specific resources in the documentation for a list of their specific sub classes and resulting URI paths.

Authentication ¶

The accessing client has to present a valid Application Name (Api-Application) and Authorization Token (Api-Token) in the HTTP header section of each request regardless of the HTTP method. API tokens can be created within suSSHi Chef by a super administrator. The super administrator can limit the allowed API accesses for a specific application (i.e. source IP addresses, suSSHi users, suSSHi targets, etc.).

Below output shows the two headers needed for every request. Throughout the following API documentation the two headers are not explicitly referenced but must be included:

Api-Token: <application-token>
Api-Application: <application-name>

Return Codes ¶

All resources respond with an HTTP return code and depending on the HTTP method, may contain data or not.

Return Code Description Body
200 OK - The request returned successful and contains data in the body Data in JSON representation
204 No Content - The request returned successful, no data response -
400 Bad Request - The request is incorrect, either the URI is wrong or the data in the body contains errors Error text in JSON representation
401 Unauthorized - Authentication failed. The API-Token / API-Application information is incorrect Error text in JSON representation
403 Forbidden - Authorization failed. The API-Token / API-Application is not allowed to access this resource Error text in JSON representation
404 Not Found - The requested resource can not be found Error text in JSON representation
409 Conflict - An uniqueness validation error occurred / the object already exists Error text in JSON representation
422 Unprocessable Entity - Please check the record for invalid attributes or types Error text in JSON representation
500 Internal Server Error -

Filters ¶

The API provides a way to narrow down the results using filters. The filters are object-specific, so please refer to the respective models for the corresponding filters.

Filters are only available for the GET method and can be combined into a query string as query parameters and attached to the URL. A query string is separated from the base URL using ? A single query parameter is always specified in the form key=value. Several query parameters are separated from each other using &:

/api/v1/config/susshi_users/logins?filter1=value1&filter2=value2...

The values can either be of type integer, boolean or string. Whenever the value is of type string, a special syntax allow to create more complex queries by prefixing a type to the string.

String Queries ¶

Prefix Description Example
begin:: String begins with given argument, case-sensitive fullname=begin::Alexander
ibegin:: String begins with given argument, case-insensitive username=ibegin::AleX
end:: String ends with given argument, case-sensitive comment=end::Testing
iend:: String ends with given argument, case-insensitive comment=iend::testing
match:: String matches on given argument, * means any character, case-sensitive ssh_key_type=match::*rsa*
imatch:: String matches on given argument, * means any character, case-insensitive email=imatch::*susshi.io
<string> Exactly match on string, case-sensitive groupname=Administrators

Common queries ¶

There are GET query-filters that can be used on all models:

Key Type Description
removable boolean Filter on objects that can be removed without violating foreign key constraints in the database

Postman Collection ¶

The easiest way to get started using the suSSHI Chef API is to use our Postman request collection. You can download the collection from here and import it into Postman.

Please define the following API Environment by providing values for the following keys:

Key Description Example
susshi_chef_api_scheme The HTTP Scheme (http, https) of the suSSHi Chef URI https
susshi_chef_api_host FQDN of the suSSHi Chef URI susshi-chef.corporate.org
susshi_chef_api_application The Application name as set under System / API Tokens application1
susshi_chef_api_token The API Token as received under System / API Tokens a7b35b2d24b560419e01e2…

Or you may download this environment template and edit it afterwards:

{
  "name": "suSSHi Chef Config API Environment",
  "values": [
    {
      "key": "susshi_chef_api_scheme",
      "value": "YOUR_SUSSHI_CHEF_API_SCHEME",
      "enabled": true
    },
    {
      "key": "susshi_chef_api_host",
      "value": "YOUR_SUSSHI_CHEF_API_HOST",
      "enabled": true
    },
    {
      "key": "susshi_chef_api_application",
      "value": "YOUR_SUSSHI_CHEF_API_APPLICATION_NAME",
      "enabled": true
    },
    {
      "key": "susshi_chef_api_token",
      "value": "YOUR_SUSSHI_CHEF_API_TOKEN",
      "enabled": true
    }
  ]
}

Retrieve the entire Config
GET/api/v1/config

Accesses ¶

The suSSHi gateway is using a rulebase to allow or deny all inbound access requests. An access rule references other suSSHi config entities (like source IP addresses, suSSHi gateway users, suSSHi targets, …) to form a single rule for the rulebase. The complete rulebase consists of an ordered list of Accesses that can be accessed either partially or completely using the accesses API path.

Position ¶

The position within the list of Accesses can be determined using the “position” parameter. This can be a position or a name of an already existing rule when creating or updating, then this Access is placed before its position. Alternatively, “top” (or “begin”) or “bottom” (or “end”) can be specified as position, then the respective Access is placed at the beginning or end of the list of Accesses.

Furthermore, the parameters “position_before” and “position_after” are available, which can be used to insert the respective Access before or after a referenced Access. Here, too, either the position or the name of an existing Access can be specified.

Filters ¶

The model-specific GET query-filters are:

Key Type Description
active boolean Filter on active (true) / non-active (false) objects
access_profile string Filter on name of Access Profile
debug_level integer Filter on debug-level
description string Filter on description field
name string Filter on elements of given name
source_ip_members_include string Filter on accesses referencing Soure-IP objects of given name
susshi_user_members_include string Filter on accesses referencing SusshiUser objects of given name
target_user_members_include string Filter on accesses referencing TargetUser objects of given name
target_members_include string Filter on accesses referencing Target objects of given name
target_fusion_members_include string Filter on accesses referencing TargetFusion objects of given name

Access Profiles ¶

The Access Profile is used by the suSSHi gateway to enforce parameters for the SSH connection. Besides controlling which SSH features are allowed (i.e. port forwards, command executes, etc.) in an SSH connection the Access Profile can also enforce session idle timeouts and maximum session length. Additionally suSSHi parameters like logging mask or hostkey learning can be altered.

Filters ¶

The model-specific GET query-filters are:

Key Type Description
name string Filter on elements of given name
description string Filter on description field

Access Profiles ¶

GET https://susshi.io/api/v1/config/profiles

Headers

Body

  {
    "id": 4,
    "name": "Full access",
    "description": "Full access and logging",
    "client_auth_set_id": 22,
    "LoggingMask": 127,
    "MaxSessionIdleSeconds": 43200,
    "MaxSessionSeconds": 86400,
    "SSHAgentForward": true,
    "SSHCommandExecs": [
      ".*"
    ],
    "SSHInteractive": true,
    "SSHSecureCopy": true,
    "SSHSecureFileTransfer": true,
    "SSHLocalForwards": [
      "localhost:*"
    ],
    "SSHRemoteForwards": [
      "localhost:*"
    ],
    "SSHSessionSubsystems": [
      "subsystem"
    ],
    "SSHSocketForward": false,
    "SSHTcpForwardSsh": false,
    "SSHX11Forward": false,
    "TargetHostKeyLearning": "prompt",
    "TargetPreferredAuthentications": [
      "keyboard-interactive",
      "password",
      "publickey",
      "publickey-ssh-agent"
    ]
  }
]

      "type": "number",
      "description": "Maximum session timer (in seconds)"
    },

      "type": "boolean",

Name of profile

Source IPs ¶

suSSHi access rules can be configured to only allow access for certain source hosts (i.e. known admin networks). The source_ips API allows to show, modify and delete the corresponding objects. Objects can either be IPv4 addresses or networks (IPv4 prefixes), IPv6 addresses or networks (IPv6 prefixes) and can also be grouped (mixed IPv4/IPv6 protocol groups are also allowed).

Filters ¶

The model-specific GET query-filters are:

Key Type Valid for Subtype Description
read_only boolean any Filter on read-only (true) / writable (false) objects
description string any Filter on description field
ip_address string Network Filter on ip_address field
name string any Filter on elements of given name
has_members boolean Group Filter on group objects that have any members
has_memberships boolean Network Filter on network objects that are part of any group

Source IP Networks and Groups ¶

GET https://susshi.io/api/v1/config/source_ips
Responses200
Headers
Content-Type: application/json
Body
{
  "nets": [
    {
      "id": 23,
      "name": "DevNet",
      "ip_address": "192.168.25.0/24",
      "description": "Developers network",
      "memberships": [
        "intranet",
        "Developers"
      ],
      "read_only": false
    }
  ],
  "groups": [
    {
      "id": 29,
      "name": "Intranet",
      "description": "Our Internet",
      "members": [
        "DevNet"
      ],
      "read_only": false
    }
  ]
}
Schema
{
  "$schema": "http://json-schema.org/draft-04/schema#",
  "type": "object",
  "properties": {
    "nets": {
      "type": "array",
      "description": "Array of Source IP network (hash) objects"
    },
    "groups": {
      "type": "array",
      "description": "Array of Source IP group (hash) objects"
    }
  }
}

suSSHi Users ¶

The suSSHi users represent the users that are connecting to the suSSHi gateway (i.e. administrative users, …) and are referenced in the suSSHi access rules. Referenced suSSHi users can either be single users that can be managed in there entirety (i.e. meta data like name or mail address, SSH publickeys, group memberships, etc.) or suSSHi user groups. Both types can be managed using the susshi_users API.

Direct management of SSH publickeys for suSSHi users is also provided using the susshi_user_keys API.

Allowed characters for the primary identifier field are as follows:

Type Identifier field Allowed Characters Comment
login username a-z A-Z 0-9 . _ - case-insensitive
group groupname a-z A-Z 0-9 . _ - : @ / \ space case-insensitive

Filters ¶

The model-specific GET query-filters are:

Key Type Valid for Subtype Description
active boolean any Filter on active (true) / non-active (false) objects
email string Login Filter on email field
fullname string Login Filter on fullname field
has_members boolean Group Filter on group objects that have any members
has_memberships boolean Login Filter on login objects that are part of any group
has_susshi_user_keys boolean Login Filter on login objects that have SusshiUserKeys
groupname string Group Filter on groupname field
username string Login Filter on username field

TOTP Parameters for suSSHi Login Users ¶

The totp_state attribute allows to control TOTP settings:

  • When set to inactive, all TOTP settings are removed from user

  • When set to active and no totp_secret attribute is provided, suSSHi Chef will create a new secret for user

  • When set to activation_pending and no totp_activation_token attribute is provided, suSSHi Chef will create a new activation token for user

Beside this, the totp_secret and totp_activation_token can be set by the API directly. The length is fixed to 32 characters. In this case, the totp_state field is updated automatically.

suSSHi Login Users and Groups ¶

GET https://susshi.io/api/v1/config/susshi_users
Responses200
Headers
Content-Type: application/json
Body
{
  "logins": [
    {
      "id": 13,
      "username": "oliver",
      "fullname": "Oliver Rauscher",
      "email": "oliver@susshi.io",
      "active": true,
      "totp_state": "inactive",
      "totp_uri": "otpauth...",
      "totp_activation_token": "FIC6ISAZPFSB5RXEGCPAHLYTPLEYCTY3",
      "memberships": [
        "developers",
        "testers"
      ],
      "susshi_user_keys": [
        {
          "id": 5,
          "title": "RSA Key",
          "public_blob": "ssh-rsa AAAAB3Nza...dw==",
          "ssh_key_type": "ssh-rsa",
          "user_id": 13,
          "username": "oliver"
        }
      ]
    }
  ],
  "groups": [
    {
      "id": 17,
      "groupname": "developers",
      "description": "The Developers",
      "active": true,
      "members": [
        "oliver",
        "jens",
        "alexander"
      ]
    }
  ]
}
Schema
{
  "$schema": "http://json-schema.org/draft-04/schema#",
  "type": "object",
  "properties": {
    "logins": {
      "type": "array",
      "description": "Array of suSSHi User Login (hash) objects"
    },
    "groups": {
      "type": "array",
      "description": "Array of suSSHi User Group (hash) objects"
    }
  }
}

suSSHi User Keys ¶

For authentication of suSSHi users to the suSSHi gateway it is possible to use SSH publickey authentication. The susshi_user_keys API allows direct management of SSH publickeys for the suSSHi users.

Filters ¶

The model-specific GET query-filters are:

Key Type Description
title string Filter on title field
fingerprint string Filter on fingerprint field
public_blob string Filter on public_blob
ssh_key_type string Filter on ssh_key_type
user_id integer Filter on SusshiUser ID field
username string Filter on SusshiUser name field

Identifier

Target Users ¶

The target users represent the target user IDs the suSSHi users are connecting to on the target systems (i.e. root, postgres, …) and are referenced in the suSSHi access rules. Referenced target users can either be single users that can be managed as individual users or as target user groups. There are also different target user types: user names, regex user names and mapping user names (please refer to suSSHi documentation). The target_user API allows management of target users as well as target user groups.

Allowed characters for the primary identifier field are as follows:

Type Identifier field Allowed Characters Comment
login username a-z A-Z 0-9 . _ - @ / \ space case-sensitive
regex name a-z A-Z 0-9 . _ - space case-sensitive
mapping name a-z A-Z 0-9 . _ - space case-sensitive
group groupname a-z A-Z 0-9 . _ - : @ space case-sensitive

Filters ¶

The model-specific GET query-filters are:

Key Type Valid for Subtype Description
description string any Filter on description field
groupname string Group Filter on groupname field
has_members boolean Group Filter on group objects that have any members
has_memberships boolean Login, Mapping, Regex User Filter on login objects that are part of any group
username string Login, Mapping, Regex User Filter on username field

Targets ¶

suSSHi targets are the target servers the suSSHi users are connecting to and are referenced in the suSSHi access rules. Reference target hosts can either be single hosts or host groups. There are also different target host types: static target hosts, dynamic target hosts, domain targets (please refer to suSSHi documentation). The target API allows management of target hosts of all types as well target host groups.

Direct management of SSH hostkeys (used for authenticating the target host) is also provided using the target_host_keys API.

Allowed characters for the primary identifier field are as follows:

Type Identifier field Allowed Characters Comment
domain domainname a-z 0-9 . - FQDN pattern
dynamic hostname a-z 0-9 . - FQDN pattern
network network (valid IP address format)
static hostname a-z 0-9 . _ - space automatically downcased, case-insensitive
group groupname a-z A-Z 0-9 . _ : / - space case-insensitive

Filters ¶

The model-specific GET query-filters are:

Key Type Valid for Subtype Description
active boolean any Filter on active (true) / non-active (false) objects
description string any Filter on description field
domainname string Target Domain Filter on domainname field
hostname string Static Host, Dynamic Target Filter on hostname field
groupname string Target Group Filter on groupname field
network string Target Network Filter on network field
proxy_realm string Target Network Filter on proxy_realm field
has_members boolean Target Group Filter on group objects that have any members
has_memberships boolean Target Domain, Dynamic Target, Target Network, Static Host Filter on objects that are part of any group
has_target_host_keys boolean Static Host, Dynamic Target Filter on objects that have TargetHostKeys
has_target_fusions boolean Static Host Filter on objects that are used in TargetFusions
has_sockets boolean Static Host Filter on objects that have sockets (IP addresses) configured

Target Host Keys ¶

The suSSHi gateway (like any SSH client) authenticates target hosts using SSH publickey authentication. The target_host_keys API allows direct management of SSH hostkeys for suSSHi targets.

Filters ¶

The model-specific GET query-filters are:

Key Type Description
fingerprint string Filter on fingerprint field
public_blob string Filter on public_blob
ssh_key_type string Filter on ssh_key_type
target_id integer Filter on Target ID field
target string Filter on Target name field

Target Fusions ¶

To use this feature, a valid subscription with this feature enabled is required.

The suSSHi Target Fusions are elements to link Target Users (Login Users) and Targets (all types) to a linked element, which can then be used in an Access Rule instead of Target User and Target. This allows a different type of combination in access rules. The individual Target Fusion Link elements can be combined into Target Fusion Groups. The target_fusions API allows to show, modify and delete the corresponding objects.

Filters ¶

The model-specific GET query-filters are:

Key Type Valid for Subtype Description
groupname string Fusion Group Filter on groupname field
target_id integer Fusion Link Filter on Target ID field
target_name string Fusion Link Filter on Target name field
target_user_id integer Fusion Link Filter on TargetUser ID field
target_user_name string Fusion Link Filter on TargetUser name field
has_members boolean Fusion Group Filter on group objects that have any members
has_memberships boolean Fusion Link Filter on link objects that are part of any group

Proxies ¶

To use this feature, a valid subscription with this feature enabled is required.

suSSHi proxies are daemons installed to allow a suSSHi gateway to connect to a target via this proxy instance. A suSSHi proxy daemon has to be deployed with the configuration received from this API or the suSSHi Chef UI and has to be able to resolve hostnames by DNS or other naming services within the destination network the proxy daemon is responsible.

Note that removing a proxy also removes all referenced targets associated with that proxy.

Filters ¶

The model-specific GET query-filters are:

Key Type Description
contact string Filter on contact field
comment string Filter on comment field
description string Filter on description field
hostname string Filter on elements of given name
port integer Filter on given port
realm string Filter on given realm
use_individual_identities boolean Filter on objects using (true) / not using (false) individual identities (autentication keys)

Bastions ¶

The suSSHi gateway is using a rulebase to allow or deny all inbound Bastion requests (to Bastion Proxies). An Bastion rule references other suSSHi config entities (like source IP addresses, suSSHi gateway users and suSSHi proxies) to form a single rule for the rulebase. The complete rulebase consists of an sortable list of Bastions that can be accessed either partially or completely using the bastions API path.

Filters ¶

The model-specific GET query-filters are:

Key Type Description
active boolean Filter on active (true) / non-active (false) objects
debug_level integer Filter on debug-level
description string Filter on description field
name string Filter on elements of given name
profile string Filter on name of Bastion Profile
proxy_members_include string Filter on bastions referencing Proxy objects of given name
source_ip_members_include string Filter on bastions referencing Soure-IP objects of given name
susshi_user_members_include string Filter on bastions referencing SusshiUser objects of given name

Position ¶

The position within the list of Bastions can be determined using the “position” parameter. This can be a position or a name of an already existing rule when creating or updating, then this Bastion is placed before its position. Alternatively, “top” (or “begin”) or “bottom” (or “end”) can be specified as position, then the respective Bastion is placed at the beginning or end of the list of Bastions.

Furthermore, the parameters “position_before” and “position_after” are available, which can be used to insert the respective Bastion before or after a referenced Bastion. Here, too, either the position or the name of an existing Bastion can be specified.

When processing the bastion rule base during an access request, the first matching rule found is used and the corresponding profile is applied.

Bastions ¶

Bastion Profiles ¶

The Bastion Profile is used by the suSSHi gateway to enforce parameters for the SSH Bastion connection.

Filters ¶

The model-specific GET query-filters are:

Key Type Description
name string Filter on elements of given name
description string Filter on description field

Operations ¶

The operations API is used to execute operational commands in regard of changed configurations. All changes to the suSSHi Databases whether on UI or through the config API have to be translated into a low latency accessible format on request. Through this API, the changes can be reviewed or listed and activated.

Pending Changes ¶

Pending changes can be requested by this resource. Return code 404 (Not found) is returned if there are no pending changes. The Pending changes contain a list of all changes made since last activation.

GET https://susshi.io/api/v1/operations/pending_changes
Responses200404
Headers
Content-Type: application/json
Body
{
  "pending_changes": 2,
  "pending_version": 119,
  "last_activation": "2018-03-22T10:41:49.103Z",
  "changes": [
    {
      "class": "Access",
      "date": "2018-03-23T05:14:12.166Z",
      "message": "Removed Source Ip Net 'Any' from Access 'Rule 0001'",
      "who": "Administrator"
    },
    {

Activate pending changes ¶

The activation of pending changes is triggered through this resource. After successful requesting the activation of pending changes, a list of activated changes is returned. This list is in the same format as for the resource List pending changes (see above).

Return code 404 (Not found) is returned if there are no pending changes.

Health Operations ¶

The health operations API can be used to retrieve health status for gateways and proxies. You must allow the API token for health operations separately from configuration operations.

Gateway Health ¶

The Gateway health status can be queried from this resource. The Gateway health status contains a list of all configured Gateways within the partition and their health status. Requesting the integrity status triggers a query of the live status of all configured Gateways. Therefore, the API should be queried less frequently to avoid a heavy load on the Gateways.

Retrieving the health status could take some time in case Gateway(s) are unreachable.

Status return ¶

Status value Description
running The Gateway is reachable and functional
unreachable The Gateway is not reachable
fatal or internal-error Something went wrong

Proxies Health ¶

The Proxy health status can be queried from this resource. The Proxy health status contains a list of all configured Proxies within the partition and their health status. Requesting the integrity status triggers a query of the live status of all configured Proxies through a Gateway. Therefore, the API should be queried less frequently to avoid a heavy load on the gateways and proxies.

Retrieving the health status could take some time in case Proxy or Proxies are unreachable.

Status return ¶

Status value Description
reachable The Proxy is reachable and functional, other values like version or ip_address are also filled with valid values
unreachable The Proxy is not reachable
unknown-proxy The Proxy is a suSSHi Proxy, but not part of this installation
not-proxy The configured Proxy is not a suSSHi Proxy, but e.g. a standard SSH server
gateway-unreachable The suSSHi Gateway is unreachable, thus the Proxy status could not be retrieved
old-gateway-version The suSSHi Gateway software version is older than 20.06.0 and not supporting Proxy status requests
fatal or internal-error Something went wrong

Validate OIDC session secret
POST/api/v1/operations/oidc/validate

Validates the secret displayed during an SSH session with OIDC authentication. During validation the AuthTicket is updated with the given JWT informations:

  • Issuer (iss)

  • Audience (aud)

  • Subject (sub)

  • Session ID (sid)

Sign the user out
POST/api/v1/operations/oidc/logout

Signs the user sessions out based on the stored information from validation step.

  • All SwiftIpCaching recorded with the matching JWT issuer, audience, sub and sid is deleted

  • If the session was created based on a Profile with an client auth set that requests the logout of running sessions, the running SSH sessions are terminated

  • All ODIC auth tickets are deleted

The logout request should contain all JWT information that was presented during validation, whereby one or both of the attributes sub or sid must be included in addition to iss and aud.
